description.value: A longitudinal fMRI study examined whether baseline BOLD response to alcohol pictures differed among college drinkers and predicted subsequent escalation to heavy drinking.

spans.text: In this longitudinal study, we ascertained whether blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) fMRI response to alcohol pictures predicted subsequent drinking among college students.

value: We hypothesized that moderate drinkers who transitioned to heavy drinking (transitioners) would show greater baseline BOLD response to alcohol images than those who remained continuously moderate drinkers within cue-reactive networks, including dorsal and ventral striatum, VMPFC, and OFC.
We also predicted that transitioners would show similar activation as individuals who were continuously heavy drinkers.

description.value: Longitudinal observational study of college students scanned at baseline and followed with monthly substance-use surveys for one year.

spans.text: Participants were forty-three 18- to 21-year-olds in the United States who underwent BOLD scanning and completed monthly substance use surveys over the following year.
Participants were divided into three groups according to baseline and 12-month follow-up drinking quantity and frequency

The final sample included 43 participants: (i) 13 moderate drinkers who drank moderately at baseline and follow-up; (ii) 14 transitioners who drank moderately at baseline, but heavily at follow-up; and (iii) 16 heavy drinkers, who drank heavily at baseline and follow-up
Total task length was 5:54
